title: Why the Ring Loses: Rolling Energy Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
A bowling ball rolls down a lane, a coin rolls off a table, a ring rolls down a slope. When Diya lets a ring, a disc and a ball go from the same height on the same slope, the ball wins and the ring comes last, every time. Why? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 6, System of Particles and Rotational Motion) we learn the kinetic energy of rolling motion. Note: rolling is not in the current rationalised NCERT book; it is in the JEE Advanced syllabus (rolling without slipping).

On a live motion notebook a ring, a disc and a ball race down a 30 degree slope while the readout shows each body's speed and how its energy splits between moving and spinning, and a graph shows three straight speed lines. A slow-mo replay freezes the race: the ring puts half its energy into spin, the disc a third, the ball two sevenths. We reason link by link why the ring loses, derive K = 1/2 mv^2 (1 + k^2/R^2) and v = root of 2gh / (1 + k^2/R^2) step by step, answer two pause-and-think questions (heavy vs light disc, rolling ball vs sliding block) and work out the energy of a rolling ball. Then the exam trap (friction does no work in rolling without slipping), an original JEE Main pattern question, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE) and PUC (Karnataka) Class 11 students, and for JEE Main, JEE Advanced and NEET preparation.
